newsitem.title: UK: European shares open lower on Wall Street factor.
newsitem.headline: European shares open lower on Wall Street factor.

text.p: UK shares opened sharply lower and other European bourses were seen falling from the outset on Friday following Wall Street's near 100-point plunge on Thursday.
Asian stock markets plummeted on Friday morning but Tokyo and Hong Kong had recovered a substantial part of the losses towards market close.
The Dow has now fallen 170 points in the past two sessions, raising fears that U.S. blue chips, which had risen nearly 30 percent this year, could be on the verge of a larger setback.
"Institutions have been reluctant to sell the past few weeks but that could change today," one London dealer said.
"The market has been expecting the Dow to come off for sometime now," one senior dealer said.
"We're (FTSE) bound to follow it lower. But since we didn't go up as much this year, we shouldn't have as hard a landing."
The FTSE 100 index was 40.3 points, or around one percent lower at 3,950.4 by 0840 GMT. The December FTSE 100 futures contract was down 46.0 points at 3,936.0.
The Frankfurt bourse, halted indefinitely by a technical fault, was expected to take another sharp blow, unable to withstand the Wall Street drag down.
"After all, it's Friday the 13th," said one Frankfurt dealer.
In Tokyo, the 225-issue Nikkei average fell by more than 500 points during the session before recovering somewhat by the close. It ended down 159.81 points, or 0.78 percent, at 20,341.39.
The Tokyo stock market could slip further if overseas investors sell their Japanese shares for short-term profits, but any losses would not be very large, brokers and analysts said.
In China, Shanghai's B share index ended down 9.267 points or 12.26 percent at 66.291 points on Friday on fears that Beijing would crack down on domestic investors trading B shares, traders said.

The fears were sparked by news reports that the securities authorities in Shenzhen had ordered local brokerages not to accept foreign exchange to buy B shares from local people unless they proved the money originated from outside China, they said.
Hong Kong stocks retraced some of Friday morning's 300-plus-point fall in afternoon trading but brokers said further downside was likely.
"This is just an overdue correction phase," said a broker with a large UK house. "Whether we fall further depends on the U.S. and I think Wall Street's correction is not yet over."
The Hang Seng Index was 241 points down at 12,811 after hitting a low of 12,736.40 in the morning session. Turnover escalated to HK$6.89 billion.
